articleTitle: Rapid Switching Strategy for Charging and Discharging Conditions of Slope Gravity Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Slope gravity energy storage system (SGESS) has the advantages of high safety, long life, no energy storage attenuation, short construction period and environmental friendliness. It has great potential to promote the consumption of new energy and the safe and stable operation of the system. During the switching process of its charging and discharging conditions, the single-channel system structure needs to undergo a shutdown-reverse start process, resulting in the energy storage system being unable to respond quickly to the dispatching needs of the power grid. At the same time, the reversal of the system will generate additional energy consumption. In response to the above problems, this paper proposes a rapid switching strategy for charging and discharging conditions based on a multichannel SGESS and builds a model to verify the effectiveness of the method. The results show that the method in this paper has no energy consumption during the switching process of charging and discharging conditions, and can quickly respond to the needs of the power grid, which verifies the effectiveness of the method. It provides new ideas for the structural construction of SGESS and is conducive to the large-scale promotion of gravity energy storage technology.

articleTitle: Research on Harmonic Detection Technology in Power Grids Based on Improved Phase-Locked Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of distributed generation into the power grid, issues such as frequency fluctuations, voltage imbalance, and harmonic distortion in power systems have become increasingly severe. Under such unbalanced and distorted grid conditions, the traditional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i_{p}-i_{q}$</tex> harmonic detection method can no longer meet engineering requirements. Addressing problems such as harmonic distortion and DC components under non-ideal grid voltage conditions, an improved <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i_{p}-i_{q}$</tex> harmonic detection algorithm is proposed. This algorithm integrates an enhanced second-order generalized integrator (SOGI) filter into the conventional ip-iq harmonic detection loop. By doing so, it enhances the ability to filter out DC components and harmonics. Simulation results demonstrate that the improved phase-locked loop (PLL) can quickly lock onto the frequency under non-ideal grid voltage conditions, while effectively filtering out high-frequency signals and DC components. Furthermore, the current distortion rate detected using the new <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i_{p}-i_{q}$</tex> algorithm is significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of High Frequency Plasma Generation System Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Under the background of the transformation and upgrading of the manufacturing industry and the rapid rise of emerging industries, new materials and new technologies have received extensive attention. Plasma discharge technology shows great potential in many fields because of its environmental friendliness and wide application. Gas/liquid phase discharge through plasma generation system is an important technical means to generate plasma. In this paper, a high-frequency plasma generation system is analyzed and designed. Firstly, the theoretical analysis and comparison of the generation structure are carried out, and the dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) with uniform structure is used. Then, the load characteristics of the two states are modeled and analyzed. The excitation part uses the power factor correction (PFC) series buck circuit and phase shifted full bridge inverter (PSFB) as the main circuit. The input voltage range is AC 110220 V, the output voltage range is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \text{kV}-20 \text{kV}$</tex>, and the output frequency is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20 \text{kHz}-50 \text{kHz}$</tex>. The wide aperture regulation of voltage and frequency is realized to meet requirements for working parameters of plasma source in DBD mode.

articleTitle: Multi-Sensor Data Fusion Method for Smart Substations Based on Hierarchical Attention Network and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The increasing complexity of modern power substations necessitates advanced data fusion techniques for intelligent monitoring, diagnosis, and decision-making. This paper proposes a novel multi-sensor data fusion framework for smart substations, leveraging hierarchical attention networks (HANs) and transfer learning techniques. The HAN effectively captures the multi-level dependencies and importances of different sensors, while transfer learning adapts the pre-trained model to specific substation environments. Extensive experiments on two real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework over state-of-the-art methods in sensor fault detection and substation state estimation tasks, achieving an average <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{F 1}$</tex>-score of 0.95 and a mean squared error of 0.018, respectively. The framework's practical applicability is showcased through case studies, highlighting its potential for intelligent monitoring, diagnosis, and decision-making in smart substations. Future research directions include incorporating additional contextual information, developing online learning mechanisms, enhancing interpretability, and exploring scalability aspects. The proposed framework represents a significant step towards revolutionizing the operation and maintenance of smart substations, contributing to a more reliable, efficient, and sustainable power grid.

articleTitle: Breeze-Driven Triboelectric-Electromagnetic Hybrid Generator for Wind Energy Harvesting and Application in Smart Weather Station
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: In distributed energy, wind turbines usually suffer from low harvesting capacity or high cut-in wind speed due to their structures. To tackle this issue, we propose a breeze-driven triboelectric-electromagnetic hybrid generator (BD-TEHG) that can efficiently harvest energy even at low wind speeds. By integrating the low-frequency adaptability of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) with the high-frequency efficiency of electromagnetic generators (EMGs), the BD-TEHG achieves optimized energy conversion across varying wind conditions. By using lightweight rotor materials and a unique wind scoop design, the generator can start at a wind speed as low as 2 m/s, ensuring effective operation in low-wind conditions. Experimental data confirm that the BD-TEHG can generate significant power, providing a consistent and reliable energy source for environmental sensors. By addressing the intermittency of renewable energy sources, reducing reliance on power grids, and minimizing battery replacement needs, this innovation provides a sustainable and efficient solution. The BD-TEHG advances the application of resilient energy systems in environmental monitoring and smart technologies, contributing to the broader utilization of wind energy under challenging conditions.

articleTitle: Construction and Application of a Full-Process Carbon Emission Measurement System for Power Based on Regional Network Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: With the widespread use of clean energy and the construction and development of the new power system, frequent interactions occur among multiple entities on the source, grid, and load sides. Traditional carbon emission measurement methods, which primarily rely on energy consumption-side statistics, can no longer meet the carbon emission management needs of regional power systems. This paper analyzes the carbon measurement indicator system, measurement methods, systems, and applications from the perspectives of power flow and carbon emission flow. First, based on the regional network structure, a carbon emission measurement indicator system for the source, grid, and load sides is established. The carbon measurement is subdivided into four stages, these stages are interconnected through boundary conditions, achieving full-process carbon emission measurement. Second, a carbon emission measurement method is proposed. Considering the spatiotemporal distribution characteristics of the carbon footprint and power flow, a carbon footprint matrix for the source, grid, and load sides is constructed. By using the carbon footprint tracking algorithm, accurate carbon emission measurement is achieved. Third, a blockchain-based full-process carbon emission measurement system for electricity is designed. A layered and zoned blockchain architecture is employed, and smart contracts are used to automate the collection, storage, and trading of carbon measurement data, ensuring the authenticity, integrity, and traceability of the carbon measurement data. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the full-process carbon emission measurement system are verified with a provincial power grid as a case study.

articleTitle: Grid-Connected Control Strategy for Photovoltaic Storage System Based on Constitutive Grid-Type Control
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: With the intensification of environmental pollution problems and the gradual depletion of traditional energy sources, renewable energy represented by wind and solar energy is growing rapidly. In this context, the problem of grid connection of optical storage system has become particularly important. In this paper, we propose a grid-connected control strategy for optical storage based on gridbased control, which can ensure stable output voltage, current and power, which does not rely on phase-locked loop (PLL) to keep synchronized with the power grid, but spontaneously synchronizes with the grid through its own control ability, which is especially important in weak power grids, because it can provide better stability and support for the power grid. Finally, the Simulink simulation platform was used to carry out the experiment. Experimental results show that the grid-connected strategy can provide stable power for the system, and can quickly restore stability under the condition of power step change.

articleTitle: Design of a Medium-Voltage Low-Power Low-Dropout Linear Regulator
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: This study presents a low-power low dropout linear regulator (LDO) design methodology for medium voltage applications. The design method is particularly targeted at the power management requirements in the medium-voltage range. By optimizing the tuned tube structure, selecting a low-power and high-gain error amplifier, implementing an efficient switching control strategy, and constructing an accurate feedback network, the design method achieves an effective reduction of the static and dynamic power consumption of the LDO under the premise of ensuring the stability of the output voltage. Experimental results show that the designed LDO exhibits excellent power consumption, output voltage stability and environmental adaptability in medium-voltage applications, and is suitable for power management requirements in portable electronic devices, precision instruments and IoT sensor nodes.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control Algorithm for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Based on Enhanced Luenberger Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The enhanced Luenberger observer-based sensorless control algorithm showcases exceptional capabilities in scenarios demanding low-speed operation and high dynamic performance. This study addresses the inherent limitations of traditional methods in rotor position and speed estimation accuracy by introducing an innovative optimization framework. The integration of nonlinear compensation and adaptive mechanisms significantly improves the observer's resilience to noise and adaptability to parameter fluctuations. Paired with an optimized model predictive current control (TV-MPCC) strategy, this advanced approach not only enhances rotor state estimation precision but also reduces algorithmic complexity. A detailed exploration, from theoretical foundation to experimental validation, underpins the design of the improved observer and its effective integration into control strategies. Results from simulations and experiments confirm that the proposed algorithm achieves consistent high-precision estimation throughout the entire speed range. Additionally, it outperforms conventional methods in terms of dynamic responsiveness, steady-state behavior, and disturbance rejection, providing a solid technological base for sensorless control in high-performance PMSM applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Adjustment Strategy for Leading Phase Ability Improvement of Doubly-Fed Induction Machines in Pumped Storage Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Pumped storage power station's leading phase operation can balance the surplus power, stabilize the voltage, achieving smooth regulation, so as to smooth the load fluctuations. The phase operation of the unit requires no additional investment, the adjustment process is smooth, and the operation is simple, which is the first choice to solve the existing reactive power surplus problem. The paper explores the limitations of the leading phase range of variable speed hydro-generating unit and proposes a novel strategy for controlling it. It establishes a mathematical model of the unit., then the coordinate transformation is carried out and the relevant control theory is put forward. The factors limiting the reactive power regulation limit of the unit are fully considered. Finally, in the limit boundary, by controlling the slip rate, the variable speed unit can reach the phase range that the constant speed unit cannot reach. This strategy not only improves the phase entry range of the pumping and storage unit, but also increases the phase entry speed.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction of Rural Power Systems with High Proportions of Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Access to a high proportion of distributed generation has become one of the essential directions of power system reform. This paper mainly studies the impact of a high proportion of distributed generation access on the construction of rural distribution networks and the corresponding solutions. By analyzing the structure and characteristics of the current rural distribution network. How can the distribution network's design and operation management be optimized to ensure its safety, stability, and economy under a high proportion of distributed generation access? A series of technical solutions are proposed to improve the adaptability of the distribution network to distributed generation access and promote the sustainable development of rural power grid construction.

articleTitle: Analysis and Prediction of Electric Vehicle Charging Supply and Demand Based on Data-Driven
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The persistent problem of charging difficulties has long been a significant factor affecting users' decisions on choosing electric vehicles (EVs). Therefore, accurately grasping and applying the charging demand information is of paramount importance for every aspect of the electric vehicle ecosystem. This study based on a real dataset of EV charging, employs data analysis and mining techniques to dissect the charging demand information embedded within it. It defines the charging demands of EVs from three aspects, analyzes their spatiotemporal characteristics, and delves deeply into the charging supply and demand situations at different charging stations. Meanwhile, neural network models are utilized to predict users' charging demands. The research reveals various patterns of user charging behaviour at different charging stations, which can indicate whether the supply and demand at these stations are balanced. It also clarifies the rational configuration directions of charging facilities in different functional areas and enables effective predictions of future charging demands at various levels. This research provides multiple parties with insights into charging demands, contributing to the improvement of resource allocation efficiency, facilitating the construction of a more intelligent and efficient charging service system, and promoting the sustainable development of the electric vehicle industry.

articleTitle: Carbon Emission Prediction on the Power Generation Side Based on the CNN-LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: As computer technology advances at a breakneck pace, its applications are becoming more and more prevalent in diverse fields. Particularly in addressing global environmental issues, computer modeling and data analysis techniques provide robust support for accurate predictions and decision-making. To address a series of issues related to global warming caused by greenhouse gases, China has proposed the “dual carbon” goals to achieve carbon emission reductions across various industries. As the single industry with the highest proportion of carbon emissions in China, the carbon reduction process of the power industry will directly affect the further realization of the “dual carbon” goals. This paper analyzes and selects the main factors affecting carbon emissions based on the carbon emission data of the power industry in a certain area from 1995 to 2022. Subsequently, it constructs a Convolutional Neural NetworksLong Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) model and a STIRPAT model. By comparing the fitting degree R2 and the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), the model with higher precision is selected for scenario prediction, resulting in forecasts of future carbon emissions from the power generation side under different scenarios.

articleTitle: Short-Term Wind Power Load Prediction Based on APSO-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Accurate prediction of wind power load can improve the stability and reliability of power grid. In this paper, an adaptive optimal PSO- LSTM neural network algorithm (APSO-LSTM) is proposed to accurately predict wind power load. Firstly, the whole particle swarm is divided into three subpopulations, and the particle evolution is carried out according to the properties and renewal mode of the particles in each subgroup, so as to ensure the diversity of the population. Secondly, adaptive algorithm is used to optimize the learning factor of PSO to improve the convergence of the algorithm and the quality of the optimal solution. Experiments show that the APSOLSTM neural network algorithm proposed in this paper has high precision for wind power load prediction.

articleTitle: Intelligent Rolling Optimization Algorithm for Day-Ahead, Intra-Day, and Real-Time Scheduling of Virtual Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The integration of Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) into modern power systems requires advanced algorithms for efficient scheduling across multiple time horizons, including day-ahead, intra-day, and real-time markets. This paper proposes an intelligent rolling optimization algorithm designed to enhance the operational efficiency and economic performance of VPPs. The algorithm combines predictive modeling, rolling optimization, and adaptive adjustments to dynamically optimize scheduling decisions while accounting for uncertainties in renewable energy generation, market prices, and demand fluctuations. By leveraging machine learning-based forecasting models and robust optimization techniques, the proposed method ensures the seamless integration of day-ahead plans with intra-day and real-time operations. Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness in improving scheduling accuracy, reducing operational costs, and enhancing system reliability under dynamic market conditions. This work provides a scalable and practical solution for intelligent VPP control in evolving electricity markets.

articleTitle: Research on Data Mining and Cost-Benefit Analysis for Large-Scale Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: In recent years, the rapid development of new energy distributed generation technology has brought great challenges to the future distribution network system. This project takes large-scale distribution network as the research object to carry out big data mining and cost-benefit optimization research. Data mining is used to improve the quantitative evaluation of QPA comprehensive benefits. Through the mapping relationship of cost-function-benefit-related parties of intelligent distribution network equipment assets Different distribution network equipment is evaluated and the benefits and costs are divided. Finally, the cost-effectiveness of intelligent distribution network is studied from two aspects: internal operation mechanism and external market mechanism. The correctness and effectiveness of this method are verified by an example analysis, and it can provide support for project investment working mode and technology selection method.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Heat and Mass Transfer Characteristic During the Natural Gas Hydrate Exploitation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: A heterogeneous hydrate reservoir model with low-permeability was constructed in this study to investigate the mechanisms of heat and mass transfer, hydrate dissociation, and capillary pressure variations during hydrate extraction using a combination of hot fluid injection and depressurization. The results show that the temperature increase in the hydrate layer was significantly lower compared to the mixed layer and the upper part of the gaseous hydrocarbon layer, indicating that horizontal hot water seepage plays a more significant role than vertical movement. Additionally, a temperature inflection point was observed in the mixed layer and the upper gaseous hydrocarbon layer. During the mid-to-late stages of extraction, a sharp rise in capillary pressure was detected near the injection well in the hydrate layer, driven by decreasing water saturation and increasing gas saturation, which enhances the potential for water lock effects in certain regions of the hydrate layer.

articleTitle: Adaptability Analysis and Optimization Algorithm for Data-Driven Virtual Power Plant Business Models
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The growing integration of renewable energy sources into modern power systems has driven the emergence of Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) as an essential concept for managing distributed energy resources. However, the adaptability of VPP business models to varying market conditions, regulatory policies, and operational uncertainties remains a critical challenge. Traditional approaches to VPP management often rely on static optimization models that struggle to cope with dynamic fluctuations in electricity prices, renewable generation output, and demand-side flexibility. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a data-driven framework for analyzing and optimizing the adaptability of VPP business models. The framework integrates machine learning techniques for predictive analytics, scenario-based simulations to evaluate business model resilience, and robust optimization algorithms for decision-making under uncertainty. By assessing key performance indicators such as profitability, operational efficiency, and risk exposure under diverse scenarios, the proposed approach enables VPP operators to make informed strategic decisions. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework effectively enhances the adaptability of VPP business models, improving economic viability and system reliability while mitigating market risks. This study provides valuable insights into the dynamic adaptation of VPPs, offering a scalable solution for the efficient and resilient integration of renewable energy into modern power grids.

articleTitle: Profit Allocation for Virtual Power Plants Based on Adaptive Optimization Algorithm and Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The operation and management of Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) require effective strategies for profit allocation and trading optimization to ensure fairness among participants and maximize overall profitability. This paper proposes a novel algorithm that integrates cooperative game theory with optimization techniques to address these challenges. The cooperative game theory framework ensures equitable profit distribution among participants based on their contributions to the VPP, while the trading optimization algorithm maximizes revenue by dynamically responding to market conditions and operational constraints. A Shapley value-based approach is employed to allocate profits fairly, reflecting each participant's marginal contribution. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method enhances participant satisfaction, ensures fairness in profit distribution, and significantly improves the economic performance of the VPP. This study provides a robust foundation for the sustainable operation of VPPs in dynamic and competitive electricity markets.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Optimization and Stability Analysis Model of Distributed Energy Resources Access in Hybrid AC/DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: AC-DC hybrid microgrid combines the high efficiency of DC microgrid with the universality of AC microgrid, which provides strong support for the flexible access and efficient utilization of Distributed Energy Resources (DER). Firstly, this paper introduces the system structure of AC-DC hybrid microgrid, including AC bus and DC bus, micro-source, energy storage device and load. Then, this paper puts forward a dynamic optimization model, aiming at improving energy utilization, reducing system loss and ensuring the stability and reliability of power supply. Through accurate modeling and cooperative control strategy, the model realizes optimal scheduling and cooperative operation among devices. In addition, the static and transient stability analysis models are established to evaluate the stability of the system under small disturbance and large disturbance. By validating both the experimental system and the simulation model, the results demonstrate that the optimized model enhances energy efficiency, minimizes system losses, and maintains power supply stability. This study offers theoretical and technical support for the continued advancement and implementation of AC-DC hybrid microgrids.

articleTitle: Unified Model and the Sliding Mode Control Method of Active Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Active power filters dynamically generate compensation currents based on load currents, reducing harmonic currents and reactive power in the power grid. The existing control methods for parallel active power filters have poor robustness, and the compensation effect is not ideal when the load current changes dramatically, especially during load switching. A control method of active power filter is proposed, which controls the compensation current and DC side voltage uniformly. Establishment of parallel active power filter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \beta$</tex> Based on the tracking control model in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \beta$</tex> coordinate system, a sliding mode control method is proposed to minimize the tracking error. The reachability of the control method is proved, and the value range of sliding mode surface parameters is determined. The simulation results show that when the THD value of the grid current is 21.54 %, the THD of the compensated grid current decreases to 3.75 %. The DC side voltage can remain stable near the reference voltage. The unified model sliding mode control method is stable and effective.

articleTitle: Early Internal Short Circuit Detection and Quantitative Assessment in Lithium-Ion Battery Packs Based on Hausdorff Distance and Charging Voltage Segment Differences
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have become ubiquitous in cutting-edge energy storage solutions. Identifying early internal short circuits (ISCs) is paramount for maintaining the safe and reliable operation of LIB systems. Hence, this paper introduces an innovative approach for early ISC detection and quantitative evaluation in LIB packs, leveraging Hausdorff distance and discrepancies in charging voltage segments. The median terminal voltage profile is extracted to depict the healthy state within the LIB pack. By integrating mean normalization with moving average filtering (MAF), discrepancies in voltage among cells are enhanced. Subsequently, Hausdorff distance is employed to identify and differentiate ISC-affected cells from healthy ones. For the identified short-circuited (SC) cells, their charging voltage segments are contrasted with those of healthy ones to estimate the SC current and resistance. Experimental findings confirm that our proposal precisely identifies SC cells within LIB packs. Notably, the minimum relative error in estimating SC resistance stands at 1.40 %, underscoring the efficacy and viability.

articleTitle: A Transient Synchronous Stabilization Control Strategy for Grid-Connected Dc Delivery System of Grid-Configured Offshore Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: As new energy sources are increasingly integrated into the power grid on a large scale, the proportion of gridconfigured offshore wind power DC delivery systems in the power system is increasing yearly. However, there is a lack of dynamic characteristics during its transient process. Therefore, this paper investigates the transient synchronous stability mechanism of grid-connected converters with virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control and proposes measures to enhance their transient stability. Firstly, the transient stability model of the offshore wind power DC sending system with VSG during grid fault is established to obtain the factors influencing the converter's transient stability under different faults. The control method of VSG is improved according to the system's voltage coupling effect. Finally, Matlab/Simulink is used to build a simulation model of the offshore wind power grid-connected model under the inaccessible fault, which demonstrates the effectiveness of the improved control method of the VSG and the active control strategy of the grid-side three-phase short-circuit fault.

articleTitle: A Dead-Time Compensation Method for SVPWM Control Inverter of PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The dead-time phenomenon may result in the distortion of the current and fluctuations in torque within the permanent magnet. Aiming at the problem, The suggestion is made for a strategy to compensate for dead-time errors while also eradicating the clamping effect of zero current. After examining the elements influencing the dead-time impact and representing the equivalent dead-time, the error voltage caused by this equivalent dead-time is balanced in a two-axis static frame using the Average dead-time compensation method. To enhance the precision in detecting current polarity, Kalman filtering is utilized to remove the high harmonics of the current under the d-q rotating shaft system, and the three-phase currents are reconstructed to determine the sector in which the stationary axis system is located to determine the compensation voltage to be applied. In addition, to enhance the caliber of the resultant current waveform, a zero-current clamping effect elimination method is incorporated into the above compensation method. Implementation of the compensation algorithm is carried out on a TMS320F28379 DSP chip, and The effectiveness of the algorithm for compensating dead-time has been verified in a system with vector control and a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive.

articleTitle: Analysis and Multi-Objective Optimization Design of Permanent Magnet Vernier Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Permanent Magnet Vernier Motors (PMVMs) have become a research hotspot in the electric vehicle industry due to their unique magnetic gear effect and high torque density. However, under low-speed and high-torque operating conditions, PMVMs face issues such as torque ripple and cogging torque-induced vibration and noise, which severely impact the motor's performance and service life. To address these issues, a detailed mathematical model of the PMVM was first established and its working principle was analyzed. Sensitivity analysis of the structural parameters identified key parameters affecting electromagnetic torque performance. Subsequently, the Central Composite Design (CCD) response surface method and Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm (MOGA) were applied to optimize these parameters, aiming to reduce torque ripple and cogging torque while enhancing the motor's efficiency and power density. The electromagnetic performance of the motor before and after optimization was verified using the finite element method. The results indicate that the optimized motor exhibits a smoother back electromotive force (EMF) waveform at the rated speed, with the total harmonic distortion reduced from 11.2% to 5.2%, significantly improving the motor's energy efficiency and operational stability.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Compensation Algorithm for Inverters Based on Hyper-Spiral Sliding Mode Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The rapid advancements in power electronics technology have made inverters, as critical components of power conversion systems, key to determining the efficiency and stability of the entire system. However, in real-world operations, inverters are often influenced by nonlinear factors such as switching dead time and the nonlinear properties of inductors and capacitors. These factors cause distortion in the output voltage waveform, thereby degrading the system's performance. To mitigate this issue, this paper introduces a nonlinear compensation method based on a hyper-spiral sliding mode observer for inverters. The observer is designed to estimate and compensate for these nonlinear errors in real time. By integrating hyper-spiral control theory, the observer significantly enhances the system's robustness and reduces sensitivity to parameter fluctuations. Simulation results indicate that the proposed nonlinear compensation method notably improves the inverter's output waveform quality and increases the system's dynamic response speed and stability. Compared to traditional sliding mode observers, the algorithm demonstrated here offers superior performance in suppressing nonlinear disturbances, providing a novel solution for high-performance inverter control.

articleTitle: Optimizing Production in Enhanced Geothermal Systems Through a Coupled Hydraulic Flow and Heat Transport Discrete Fracture Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: China's substantial hot dry rock geothermal reserves can be better exploited using Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS). Modelling Enhanced Geothermal Systems is a key approach in predicting geothermal energy production and further optimizing the management of geothermal resources. However, exploiting geothermal energy often involves interactions among physical processes such as groundwater flow, heat conduction, and heat convection in fractured porous rocks, which is challenging. Using a discrete fracture model, we simulate the coupled processes of hydraulic flow and heat transport in this study, which is solved using the open-source software OpenGeoSys. The findings reveal that increasing the injection flow rate can achieve higher energy production, but it will also shorten the lifespan of EGS. The lifespan of EGS increases linearly with the well distance. Reducing the injection flow rate can also extend the lifespan. Optimal inter-well distance and injection flow rate were identified through multi-combination simulations. Our findings provide a reference for optimizing parameters in practical EGS applications, offering a more scientific and efficient approach to geothermal energy development.

articleTitle: Technological Optimization of Smart Operation Platforms for Virtual Power Plants Based on a Cloud-Edge-Endpoint Collaborative Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The rapid integration of distributed energy resources and renewable energy systems into modern power grids has necessitated the development of intelligent operation platforms for Virtual Power Plants (VPPs). This study explores the technological optimization of a VPP smart operation platform based on a cloud-edge-endpoint collaborative architecture. The proposed architecture leverages cloud computing for centralized data analysis and optimization, edge computing for real-time decision-making and control, and endpoint devices for local monitoring and execution. Key challenges such as data transmission latency, resource allocation, and system scalability are addressed through innovative algorithms and optimization techniques. The framework ensures efficient coordination across all layers, enabling the VPP to enhance operational efficiency, reliability, and scalability. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in resource utilization, system responsiveness, and overall performance, providing a practical solution for the intelligent management of VPPs in dynamic energy environments.

articleTitle: Research on Online Parameter Identification Strategy for Brushless DC Motors Based on Model Reference Adaptive Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of industrial automation, brushless DC motors (BLDCMs) have gained widespread application across various domains, such as industrial production and household electronics. However, fluctuations in motor parameters caused by external conditions and load changes can adversely impact system stability and performance. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel online parameter identification approach based on the Model Reference Adaptive System (MRAS) algorithm, aiming to optimize motor parameter tracking in real time. Initially, a comprehensive mathematical model for BLDCMs is developed, and the effects of parameter variations on dynamic performance are analyzed in depth. Subsequently, a reference adaptive system is designed, employing real-time voltage and current signals as input data to dynamically adjust the motor model parameters for alignment with actual operational states. The simulation results validate the proposed method's effectiveness, showcasing its capability to achieve precise parameter tracking, swift dynamic response, and strong resilience in complex operating conditions, thus laying a solid foundation for high-accuracy motor control systems.

articleTitle: Vertical Gravity Energy Storage System Multi-Machine Load Distribution Strategy Based on Stochastic Simulation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Vertical gravity energy storage system(GESS) realizes high efficiency energy storage through the design of multi-unit structure, but faces the challenges of mechanical loss and conversion efficiency, using computer algorithms to optimize the operation of the system can improve the system's ability to sense and operate efficiently, providing effective support for the efficient operation of gravity energy storage., and generally ignores the influence of multi-machine system loss when load allocation of multi-machine system is carried out, in order to address the above problems, this paper proposes a stochastic simulation method of load allocation strategy, which comprehensively considers the variable and invariant losses of GESS to complete the load allocation of vertical gravity storage multi-machine system and improve the system operation efficiency. The load allocation of vertical gravity energy storage multi-machine system is accomplished by considering both variable and invariant losses. Example results show that this paper's method can improve the system efficiency by about 0.1 % to 0.25 % compared with the conventional average load allocation method, which verifies the validity of this paper's method and provides a new idea for the operation optimization of vertical gravity energy storage multi-computer system, which will help the large-scale commercial promotion of GESS in the future.

articleTitle: Electrical Load Prediction Based on Integrated Learning GBDT Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The development of the national economy is closely linked to the production of electric energy, and excessive or insufficient production has a significant impact on the operational stability of the power system. Accurate load forecasting technology holds great practical significance in the context of an expanding power grid. Traditional load forecasting methods struggle to meet the demands of power grid regulation. To enhance the predictive performance of the conventional Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) algorithm, this paper employs a regression tree model to forecast four types of short-term power loads: predictions using the CART algorithm, predictions based on a single regression model utilizing the GBDT algorithm, power load forecasts based on time series and the GBDT algorithm, and predictions that additionally consider the inclusion of an influencing factor (temperature). The results show that the 37 days average absolute error, absolute deviation mean error and quadratic deviation mean error are reduced by 2.1 %, 38.9 % and 62.33 %, respectively, compared with the single base learning model. The model has good prediction accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: Optimization and Scheduling of Wind-Photovoltaic-Integrated Energy System Based on ISSA
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: A multi-objective scheduling model of the park integrated energy system (PIES) with an improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (ISSA) is proposed for the problem of economy, stability, and environmental protection of PIES containing photovoltaic cells, wind turbines, and batteries. PIES includes three kinds of electricity, heat, and gas loads, as well as coal-fired units, gas units, wind, and photovoltaic power generation units. Aiming at the economic dispatching problem of PIES by dispatching model of PIES of the park is carried out. Economic cost and utilization rate of clean energy are taken as objective functions. The ISSA algorithm is used to solve the multi-objective function, and the example analysis shows that the proposed model is conducive to reducing the total cost of system operation. The result of the example verifies the feasibility, superiority, and applicability of ISSA in solving the multi-objective optimal scheduling store.

articleTitle: Line Loss Prediction Method for Urban Distribution Networks Based on Optimized RBF and K-means++ Algorithm Under Double Carbon Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The application of digital technology to optimize urban distribution networks and lower carbon emissions has drawn more attention as a result of the dual carbon targets and the quick development of artificial intelligence. In order to reduce the carbon emissions of urban distribution networks under the dual carbon target, a strategy for urban distribution networks based on K-means++algorithm has been proposed. The study combines improved particle swarm optimization algorithm for parameter optimization of radial basis function network. It also combines the K-mean++ algorithm to classify and manage the user line loss by time period. In this way, the goal of indirect emission reduction can be achieved. The outcomes revealed that the line loss prediction model has significant advantages in prediction accuracy compared to the comparative model, and can better capture the dynamic changes in electricity demand. After being applied in State Grid Chengdu Power Supply Company, the carbon emissions of the distribution network from July to December were significantly reduced, with the total carbon emissions and carbon emissions caused by line losses reduced to 60000 tons and 51000 tons, 55000 tons and 46750 tons, respectively. This provides new theoretical support for achieving the dual carbon goals and optimizing carbon emission management in power enterprises.

articleTitle: Research on PV Module Price Prediction Based on VMD-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: As the utilization of fossil fuels and environmental pollution increase, countries are actively promoting the use of clean energy sources such as solar and wind power. However, due to supportive policies and the low barriers to entry in the photovoltaic (PV) industry, there is intense competition among PV manufacturers, leading to a reduction in the prices of PV modules. To foster the healthy development of the PV industry and ensure fairness and justice within the sector, this paper establishes a VMD-SSA-LSTM forecasting method. First, VMD (Variational Mode Decomposition) is used to decompose the price information of PV modules; second, SSA (Singular Spectrum Analysis) is applied to optimize the parameters within the LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) network; finally, the method combines historical prices of components such as solar cells and photovoltaic glass to predict the future prices of the modules. The experimental results indicate that the forecasting method developed in this paper has high accuracy and can provide guidance for the future development of the PV industry, thus promoting the development and utilization of solar energy.

articleTitle: Dual End Grid Control Strategy for Offshore Wind Power Grid-Connected MMC-HVDC System Considering DC Line Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of the scale of offshore wind power, its grid-connected access puts forward higher requirements for the stability and reliability of the power grid. High voltage direct current (HVDC) systems, primarily modular multilevel converter (MMC) technology, are ideal for offshore wind power grid integration due to their high efficiency, reliability and flexibility. However, the inherent parasitic losses in long-distance DC transmission lines substantially degrade system operational efficiency. To address this challenge, this study develops a bipolar control architecture for offshore wind-integrated MMC-HVDC systems, explicitly incorporating line loss dynamics into the control loop design. This strategy significantly improves the power transmission efficiency by optimizing the power control at the wind farm end and the land access end, combined with the loss compensation mechanism of the DC line. The proposed control strategy can improve the power transmission efficiency of the system by 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> to 6% compared to the legacy control strategy, with concurrent preservation of system dynamic stability and functional reliability.

articleTitle: Evaluation Model of Safe Operation of Distribution Network Supported by User-Side Energy Storage Based on Entropy Weight-Grey Correlation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a user-side energy storage (USES) supporting distribution network safe operation evaluation model based on entropy weight -grey correlation method to improve the efficiency and accuracy of safe operation evaluation of USES system in distribution network. The paper first constructs an operation index library of electrochemical energy storage (ES) power station, covering multiple dimensions such as power, energy efficiency, reliability and operation and maintenance costs, to provide support for the evaluation system. Then, based on the coupling relationship between the USES system and the distribution network system, a safe operation evaluation index system of the USES system on the distribution network side is constructed. Finally, based on the comprehensive evaluation model of grey correlation entropy weight method, a comprehensive evaluation of the safe operation of USES is achieved. The results show that the model can effectively evaluate the safe operation status of the USES system and support the stable and efficient operation of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Algorithm Fusion and Deep Learning Models for Power Consumption Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Accurate power load forecasting is a critical element in ensuring the safe and economic operation of power grids. However, the nonlinear characteristics of load data and abrupt operational conditions pose significant challenges to forecasting. This study proposes a forecasting method based on a Long Short-Term Memory-Gated Recurrent Unit (LSTMGRU) hybrid deep learning architecture, designed with a multiscale spatiotemporal feature extraction module. Through parallel convolutional structures and graph convolutional networks, effective load feature extraction is achieved. An adaptive weighted combined loss function is constructed to optimize the model training process, and a Stacking strategy is employed to integrate various base algorithms to improve generalization performance. The feature extraction module incorporates attention mechanisms to enhance the capture of key spatiotemporal features, while residual connections are utilized to mitigate the vanishing gradient problem. Experimental results demonstrate that this method exhibits excellent forecasting performance under various load conditions, particularly during load fluctuations, with strong adaptability. Through comparative analysis with traditional methods and other deep learning models, the advantages of this method in terms of prediction accuracy and model stability are validated, providing a new technological solution for power system load forecasting.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction and Application of the Carbon Footprint Model of Cable Products Based on the Life Cycle Assessment Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: With the proposition of the global “dual carbon” goals, achieving low-carbonization has emerged as the core imperative for the sustainable development of the power industry. As a core component in power transmission, the carbon emissions at each stage of the cable's full life cycle ought to be evaluated systematically and scientifically to meet the urgent demands of low-carbon development. This paper initiates from the six key links in the full life cycle of cable products: raw material acquisition, raw material transportation, production and manufacturing, product transportation, product usage, and decommissioning and recycling. It conducts in-depth research on the carbon footprint model and builds a comprehensive carbon emission factor library. Through quantitative analysis of the carbon emissions of cable products from “cradle” to “grave”, a precise assessment of their carbon footprints is carried out. The research outcomes are intended to offer theoretical underpinnings and practical guidance for the low-carbon transformation of the power industry. Through technological innovation approaches and process optimization measures, it helps to refine the carbon emission management of cable products.

articleTitle: Typical Load Clustering and Feature Extraction Algorithm Considering Class Imbalance
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The imbalance severely constrains the generalization ability and feature representation effectiveness of models. a research strategy for a typical load clustering and feature extraction algorithm that considers class imbalance is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a hierarchical and multi-level control architecture is constructed. By analyzing the classification characteristics of adjustable load resources, a multi-level aggregation standard technical framework is designed to achieve source-load coordinated optimization. Secondly, dynamic time warping is used to quantify the morphological differences of load curves, and a multi-agent electricity consumption behavior model is established by integrating the analysis of spatiotemporal heterogeneity under market competition mechanisms. Then, the range normalization method is employed to normalize the dimensions of typical users. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed load control strategy can ensure the tracking effect of aggregated load power to the target power, providing a reliable basis for the refined operation of power systems and demonstrating significant engineering application value.

articleTitle: Numerical Error Analysis and Improvement Methods for Streamer Discharge Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: In the field of discharge research for electrical equipment, the microscopic mechanisms of streamer discharge are difficult to obtain through experiments. Numerical simulations, however, provide an effective approach to solving this issue. Traditional numerical methods in streamer discharge simulations often face problems such as large discretization errors, numerical oscillations, and high computational resource demands, which affect the accuracy and efficiency of the simulation results. To address these issues, this study introduces an efficient numerical method that combines the reduced-order element finite element method with an adaptive mesh strategy. By utilizing the open-source numerical computation library FEniCSx, this approach enables point-wise estimation and control of numerical errors in streamer discharge simulations, offering a more efficient and accurate numerical solution strategy for discharge simulations of complex electrical equipment. In the future, the proposed method could be further extended to more complex time-varying processes and three-dimensional problems, exploring a broader range of application scenarios.

articleTitle: Construction of Smart Grid Optimization Dispatching System Based on Improved YOLOv5 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: In actual operation, the power grid faces the problems of high loss rate and long power outage time. This paper builds an optimized dispatching system to address these problems. This paper first optimizes the YOLOv5 algorithm, and then introduces a four-scale feature fusion structure to improve the object detection effect by fusing deep semantics with shallow semantic information. The Transformer encoder module is embedded in the C3 module to strengthen the correlation between pixel blocks and improve the model's performance against complex backgrounds and target occlusion. The CIoU loss function is also used in this paper, taking into account factors such as the shape of the object. Based on the optimized YOLOv5 algorithm, this paper builds an optimized dispatching system for smart grids. The data acquisition module collects images and load data of the equipment, the image processing module preprocesses the image, the equipment recognition module uses the improved YOLOv5 algorithm to identify the equipment, the load detection module calculates the load situation based on the recognition results, and the optimized dispatching module formulates the optimal dispatching strategy based on the load situation. The system based on the improved algorithm has achieved significant improvements in grid loss rate and annual average power outage time compared to the system under the traditional algorithm. The average loss rate has been reduced to 3.2704%, and the annual average power outage time does not exceed 5.83 hours, effectively improving the operating efficiency and safety of the power grid.

articleTitle: Research on Uncertainty Modeling and Optimization Trading Algorithms in the Electricity-Carbon Coupled Market
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The integration of carbon trading with electricity markets has created a complex coupled market structure, where uncertainties in renewable energy generation, market prices, and carbon quotas pose significant challenges to efficient trading. Traditional market-clearing mechanisms struggle to handle the stochastic nature of renewable power generation and the volatility of carbon prices, leading to inefficiencies in trading decisions and carbon compliance strategies. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a comprehensive framework for uncertainty modeling and optimization trading in electricity-carbon coupled markets. The framework leverages robust stochastic optimization techniques to model uncertainties in renewable energy output, electricity price fluctuations, and carbon quota dynamics, thereby enhancing decision-making accuracy and improving trading strategies. A risk-aware, adaptive trading algorithm is developed to maximize profit while ensuring compliance with carbon emission constraints and system reliability. The proposed algorithm integrates data-driven forecasting models, stochastic programming, and real-time market adjustments to dynamically respond to changes in both electricity and carbon markets. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework effectively mitigates risks associated with uncertainty, enhances economic efficiency, and ensures carbon compliance, leading to improved overall market stability. This research provides valuable insights for promoting the synergy between electricity and carbon markets under dynamic and uncertain conditions, offering a scalable and practical solution for future low-carbon power market development.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Urban and Electric Power Big Data Economy on Pollution Reduction and Carbon Reduction Based on Benchmark Regression Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Currently, in promoting ecological civilization construction in China, the coordinated governance of pollution and carbon reduction is regarded as the core strategy and implementation focus. As a new economic transformation and upgrading model, the Electric power big data economy is becoming essential in promoting this process. The entropy method is used to construct evaluation indicators for the Electric power big data economy, pollution reduction, and carbon reduction. Subsequently, a benchmark regression model was built for testing based on carefully considering other variables that may affect pollution reduction and carbon reduction through benchmark regression analysis. Finally, exploring the diversity and specificity of the impact of the Electric power big data economy on pollution reduction and carbon reduction from different dimensions - regional economic differences, Electric power size classification, and specific backgrounds of each city's development stage aims to provide targeted strategic recommendations for policymakers, ensuring the coordinated promotion of the healthy development of Electric power big data economy and environmental protection goals.

articleTitle: Intelligent Operation and Maintenance Approach for Distribution Rooms Based on Condition and Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent operation and maintenance approach for distribution rooms based on condition and risk assessment, aiming to address the issues of low efficiency, slow fault response, high maintenance costs, and the inability to promptly identify potential equipment faults in traditional distribution room operation and maintenance. The method employs Pearson correlation coefficients and Granger causality analysis to conduct correlation and causality analyses on equipment operation data, thereby identifying the key factors affecting equipment status. Subsequently, a time-series analysisbased equipment status prediction model is constructed to forecast the future status of equipment. The effectiveness of the intelligent operation and maintenance system is verified through actual case studies in conjunction with the architecture and functions of the intelligent operation and maintenance platform. The results demonstrate that intelligent operation and maintenance technology can significantly enhance the maintenance efficiency of distribution rooms and reduce fault risks and maintenance costs. The optimized operation and maintenance strategy leads to a noticeable decrease in the risk values of electrical equipment. This research strongly supports the modernization and intelligent management of distribution rooms, improves power systems' safety and economic benefits, and promotes technological progress in the power operation and maintenance industry.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Error Correction of Electric Energy Meters Using Adaptive Wavelet Packet Decomposition and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs)
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: High-precision correction of dynamic errors in electric energy meters is a key technical challenge to ensure measurement accuracy. Traditional methods face issues of insufficient feature extraction capability and limited nonlinear correction effects when dealing with dynamic error characteristics. To address these challenges, a fusion algorithm based on Adaptive Wavelet Packet Decomposition (AWPD) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) is proposed. AWPD is used to extract multi-scale features of the error signal, achieving adaptive decomposition of the signal through entropy criteria. GANs leverage the adversarial mechanism between the generator and discriminator to achieve nonlinear error correction. Experimental results demonstrate the outstanding performance of this fusion model under various operating conditions. Under light-load conditions, the mean error is reduced from 0.15 % to 0.02 %, and the standard deviation of the error is reduced from 0.08 % to 0.01 %. Under random operating conditions, even in high-noise environments, the peak error after correction is reduced from 0.48 % to 0.07 %. Furthermore, the model achieves a correction accuracy rate of over 95 % under complex operating conditions such as full load and load fluctuations, demonstrating strong robustness and adaptability. In summary, the fusion model based on AWPD and GANs can significantly improve the accuracy and stability of dynamic error correction, providing an efficient and reliable solution for dynamic error correction in electric energy meters and exhibiting good prospects for engineering applications.

articleTitle: An Optimal Decision-Making Method for Offshore Wind Power Considering Multiple Transmission Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: With the increasing scale of offshore wind farms and the diversification of power transmission technologies, selecting the most suitable transmission scheme requires a comprehensive analysis of technical feasibility, economic efficiency, and grid adaptability. This paper investigates various offshore wind power transmission methods, including highvoltage alternating current (HVAC), high-voltage direct current (HVDC), and hybrid HVAC/HVDC systems. A multi-objective decision-making framework is proposed, incorporating factors such as transmission distance, power capacity, system reliability, reactive power compensation, and overall economic cost. A case study of a deep-sea wind power cluster in China is presented to evaluate five different transmission schemes. The results demonstrate that while each transmission method has unique advantages and limitations, hybrid HVAC/HVDC transmission offers a balanced solution in terms of reliability, technical complexity, and cost-effectiveness. The proposed decisionmaking model provides a valuable reference for optimizing offshore wind power transmission strategies, contributing to the development of low-carbon, intelligent energy systems.

articleTitle: Investigation of Energy Efficiency Accounting and Project Levels of Data Centres Based on “Dual Carbon” Objective
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The assessment and analysis of energy efficiency levels offer both theoretical frameworks and practical assistance for developing strategies aimed at energy conservation and emission reduction in projects. Moreover, it is essential for the sustainable development of project plans. This study initiates by outlining the relationship between energy consumption and carbon emissions within the framework of a regional data center project. The analysis subsequently evaluates the project's energy consumption through the principles and applications of energy conservation in various systems, including power supply, lighting, and HVAC. Energy consumption is subsequently assessed, and energy efficiency levels are evaluated based on annual comprehensive energy consumption, annual comprehensive energy consumption increment, and key energy efficiency indicators. A model for optimization evaluation is developed to assess the effects of the project's new energy consumption and the intensity of energy use in the city. The research offers a reference and guidance for the preparation of reports on the project's power supply scheme to achieve further the reduction of 'power supply + energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Prediction Based on SVR-PSO-BP
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The power generation of Photovoltaic (PV) fully influenced by the meteorological factors, such as intermittent, unstable and low energy density, etc., causing power grid disequilibrium or light abandonment problems. PV generation rate prediction is an important method to overcome these shortages of PV generation system. The SVR-PSO-BP algorithm is proposed to predict photovoltaic power generation based on different meteorological characteristics and mechanisms that affect photovoltaic power generation. The research object is a ground PV power station for 1.5 MWp. 2 years' meteorological data and power generation data of this station are taken as input data to study its solar irradiance, PV power generation, environmental temperature, and other key characteristics. Using path analysis and grey correlation analysis for data preprocessing, combined with adaptive OPS-GA-PB based short-term photovoltaic power generation prediction algorithm. Using Matlab, the algorithm is implemented. And the algorithm training is applied to get a higher fitting forecasting model. The results show that both solar irradiance and temperature have an effect on PV generation rate, and solar irradiation is the main effect factor. The prediction accuracy of the training set is about 93%, and the prediction accuracy of the actual test set is over 97%. The weather forecast model can be used to predict the before-oneday and within-one-day PV generation in sunny weather. Accurate and timely prediction of photovoltaic power generation is helpful for the advanced dispatch of the power grid.

articleTitle: Optimization of Intelligent Algorithm Applications in the Transformation of Electric Power System's Energy Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: As the cornerstone of national economic development, the development level of its industry directly reflects the country's economic level and residents' living standard. As the exploitation of non-renewable resources approaches the limit, the problem of energy price rise is becoming increasingly serious. Reasonable planning and utilization of renewable energy to replace non-renewable energy has become a key topic to be solved in the power industry. This paper discusses the research and development status of multi-objective optimal dispatching in power system, and focuses on the application effect of multi-objective short-term optimal dispatching based on fuzzy satisfaction core in water and fire ionization system. This method optimizes the distribution model according to the multi-time and multi-target expected value of the power load, aiming to realize the reasonable configuration of water, heat and electricity output, meet the technical requirements of all parties, and implement the unified dispatching of the power system. This paper reviews the research process of the optimal scheduling of power system since the 1980s, including the joint optimization of system, the method of large-scale system decomposition and the coordination, and the short-term optimization of water-fire system, etc., and points out the new opportunities and challenges brought by the reform of power system since the 21st century. In addition, it also discusses the establishment of independent dispatching and managed feed-in tariff mechanism in China's electricity market bidding, and how to integrate market roles and macro control to solve existing problems. The research results of this paper provide technical support for the actual operation of electric power enterprises in the new era.

articleTitle: Flexible Load-Driven Multi-Objective Cooperative Scheduling Framework for Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Traditional load management methods have become inadequate to cope with the complex and ever-changing load demands in modern power grids. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a flexible load integration multiobjective optimization scheduling method based on distributed networks. The research method in this paper first centrally controls flexible loads through distributed networks, utilizing advanced communication technologies and intelligent control strategies to achieve precise regulation of various load resources. The multiple controllable loads are classified and modeled according to the power physical characteristics of adjustable load resources, to fully exploit their regulation potential. By establishing a multi-objective optimization model and comprehensively considering multiple objectives of grid operation, this paper proposes a scheduling idea based on chance-constrained programming. This method can solve for the optimal load scheduling scheme through optimization algorithms under the premise of meeting the operational constraints of the power grid, thereby ensuring the user's power consumption experience.

articleTitle: Real-Time Simulation and Optimization of High-Voltage Cable Construction Process Using Digital Twin and Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: The construction of high-voltage cable systems involves complex processes that require precise planning, monitoring, and optimization to ensure efficiency and reliability. This study introduces a real-time simulation and optimization framework for the high-voltage cable construction process, leveraging predictive modeling and optimization algorithms. The proposed framework integrates physical and virtual environments to create a dynamic and interactive simulation system. By utilizing real-time data acquisition, advanced predictive models, and optimization techniques, the framework enables continuous monitoring, scenario analysis, and adaptive decision-making during construction. Key challenges such as resource allocation, risk assessment, and schedule optimization are addressed through these computational methods, ensuring improved construction quality and reduced project delays. Experimental results demonstrate the framework's capability to enhance process efficiency, minimize risks, and provide valuable insights for construction management. This work highlights the potential of predictive modeling and optimization algorithms in transforming high-voltage cable construction practices.

articleTitle: Research on Enhancing Security and Energy Efficiency of Smart Grid Distribution Systems Through the Integration of Environmentally-Friendly Gas Insulation Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Traditional sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) gas is gradually limited due to its high greenhouse effect, making insulation technology become an important development direction of smart grid distribution system. Aiming at the demand of power distribution system security and energy efficiency optimization, the optimization scheme of smart grid power distribution system is proposed by combining with improved ant colony algorithm. The performance of fault location, path optimization and load balancing is improved by multi-objective optimization method. The results show that the IACO algorithm performs well in fault location time, which decreases from 85.4 seconds to 52.9 seconds, and the efficiency increases by 38.1%. The fault isolation efficiency is improved to 31.4%, which is much higher than other algorithms. The optimization rate of the system energy efficiency is 18.6%, which significantly reduces the power loss. Load balance improvement rate increased to 20.3%, effectively reducing the operating pressure of high-load nodes. Through intelligent optimization algorithm, the research can realize multi-dimensional improvement of the safety, energy efficiency and environmental friendliness of smart grid distribution system, and provide new solutions for the green development of modern power grid.

articleTitle: Analysis of Technical Parameters of Small Neutral Reactors for Three Main Transformers in 500kV Jinzhou Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: In order to cope with the potential risks in the operation of the main transformer of 500 kV Jinzhou Substation, it is planned to install a reactor in the main transformer neutral point. In this paper, using the EMTP (Electro - Magnetic Transients Program) electromagnetic transient simulation program, the over-voltage and insulation coordination are studied by installing a small reactor in the main transformer neutral point in order to determine the technical parameter selection scheme of the main transformer refitted with small reactance equipment and other targeted improvement measures are also proposed, strive to reduce the risk of zero-sequence protection action in the 500 kV Jinzhou Substation's main transformer common winding, improve the opening capacity of zero-sequence voltage for failure protection and effectively limit the short-circuit current level, earnestly ensure the safe, stable and efficient operation of the power system.

articleTitle: Intelligent Identification of Electric Meter Failures Based on Convolutional Neural Networks and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Clean Energy Storage and Power Engineering (CESPE)
abstract: Accurate detection of electric meter failures is of great significance for the efficient operation and troubleshooting of power grids. In response to the high-dimensional, temporal, and diverse fault characteristics of electric meter data, a joint detection model based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks is proposed. This model utilizes CNN to extract local spatial features and combines LSTM to capture temporal dependencies, thereby achieving efficient classification of complex fault patterns. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a classification accuracy of 91.7 % on a real electric meter failure dataset, significantly outperforming comparison models such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests (RF), and CNN-GRU. The model exhibits high robustness in key indicators such as fault detection rate (93.2%) and false alarm rate (5.2 %). Meanwhile, it maintains strong real-time performance during large-scale data processing, with an average inference time of 0.97 milliseconds per sample and a system throughput of 1030 samples per second. In summary, the CNN-LSTM joint model, leveraging its efficient feature extraction and temporal modeling capabilities for complex characteristics, provides an effective solution for intelligent detection of electric meter failures and demonstrates significant potential for engineering applications.
